key_insight: The paper introduces an unfitted boundary algebraic equation approach for 2D Stokes flow that represents the solution using lattice Green’s functions on a staggered grid and stabilizes the boundary system with a discrete Calderón preconditioner.
engineering_relevance: It enables accurate Stokes simulations in irregular geometries without body-fitted meshes or singular quadrature, making it attractive for complex-fluid and microscale flow solvers.
method: Builds velocity/pressure lattice Green’s functions from free-space Laplace LGFs.
Imposes boundary conditions at cut points via local interpolation on thin staggered boundary layers.
Uses a componentwise discrete Calderón preconditioner with FFT-based convolutions and GMRES.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports second-order convergence for velocity and pressure, discrete divergence at solver tolerance, successful tests on multiply connected domains and narrow gaps, and orders-of-magnitude condition-number reduction.
watch_item: The preconditioner remains effective but more demanding for narrow-gap and fine-grid interior problems, which may increase computational cost and implementation complexity.
paper_title: An unfitted boundary algebraic equation method with Calderón preconditioning for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometry
